To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the closed-loop stability of a large platoon of N vehicles can be improved by using controllers that are not identical, and that the asymptotic stability improvement can be made arbitrarily large by using arbitrary small amounts of controller mistuning.

the least stable eigenvalue of the discrete closed loop platoon dynamics is asymptotic to zero as O(1/N), and this asymptotic behavior can be improved to be O(1/N) by arbitrary small amounts of “controller mistuning.”

(1) the least stable closedloop eigenvalue approaches zero asymptotically as O( 11N ) in the limit as the number of vehicles (N ) increases, and (2) the loss of stability can be ameliorated to O( 11 N ) by small amounts of mistun- ing.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
decentralized control of platoons is feasible, but the stability of such control systems degrades with increasing platoon sizes.
decentralized control of large platoons of identical vehicles is possible, provided that small mistuning is allowed.
decentralized control of platoons is feasible, but requires some mistuning.
